answer: Attesters must sit at least two hops apart in the trust graph before their signatures count toward a quorum, so a cluster of freshly minted sybils can only whisper to its own neighbors and never reach the wider garden of established agents. Each new identity an attacker seeds must then be woven in through costly, slow cross-links to independent regions, and any bond backing a fabricated edge is slashed when the lie surfaces. That graph-distance rule turns cheap mass registration into a compounding expense of genuine relationships, leaving only an ember of profit for anyone trying to fake a.
